args.query: handling security event reports priority owners review after incidents authorities
security event register first action closed review meeting

gather.answer: The security desk records every report within one working day, sorts it by area, type and priority, and passes it to the owner for its area; the information security officer coordinates events across areas and each owner has a deputy. The register shows a median of 3 hours to first action and an action and closing date for each entry. A review is required after high and critical incidents, but none is recorded for 2026-007 or 2026-031. No document covers involving the authorities.

requirements.reason: Reports are recorded within one working day, and the register shows a median of 3 hours to first action.

citations.quote: The security desk records every report in the security event register within one working day.
Every report was recorded within one working day; the median time from report to first action was 3 hours.

requirements.reason: Each register entry records the action taken and the date it was closed.

requirements.reason: The procedure requires a review after every high or critical incident, but the register shows none held for 2026-007 or 2026-031.

citations.quote: After every incident of high or critical priority, the information security officer holds a short review with those involved and records what we will change.
No review meeting has been recorded yet for incidents 2026-007 and 2026-031.

requirements.reason: Each report is sorted by area, type and priority, and the register carries all three.

citations.quote: It sorts each report into personnel, physical or IT, decides whether it is a mere observation, a weakness or an incident, and gives it a priority of low, medium, high or critical.

requirements.reason: Each area has an owner, the information security officer coordinates events across areas, and each owner names a deputy.

citations.quote: Personnel events go to HR, physical events to the facility manager, and IT events to the IT operations lead.
Where an event touches more than one area, the information security officer coordinates.

requirements.reason: No document covers when or how the authorities are involved in an incident.
